keywords.def: several or many; used to add credibility to what you are saying
used to encourage people to move or look away from something, or to stop them from paying it much attention
take control of something that does not belong to you for your own advantage
completely fail to notice or realise the threat of something
teach somebody to think or behave in a new or different way

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《6分钟英语》。

sentences.en: I’m Neil. And I’m Beth. In our lifetime, 1 in 5 people will be affected by cancer, a disease where cells grow uncontrollably and cause tumours in the body.
sentences.zh: 我是Neil。我是Beth。在我们的一生中，五分之一的人会受到癌症的影响，这是一种细胞不受控制地生长并在体内引起肿瘤的疾病。

sentences.en: Tumours can be benign, meaning not cancerous, or malignant, meaning cancerous, and in 2022 there were an estimated 9.7 million deaths from malignant cancers worldwide.
sentences.zh: 肿瘤可以是良性的，也就是非癌性的，也可以是恶性的，也就是癌性的。据估计，2022年全球有970万人死于恶性肿瘤。

sentences.en: But in this programme, we’ll be focusing on some good news instead.
sentences.zh: 但在本期节目中，我们将把重点放在一些好消息上。

sentences.en: Vaccines are medicine which protect the human body by making it immune from a certain disease.
sentences.zh: 疫苗是一种药物，通过使人体对某种疾病产生免疫力来保护人体。

sentences.en: Now, there’s been a sudden and important discovery – a breakthrough - in the development of a new vaccine called mRNA.
sentences.zh: 现在，一种名为mRNA的新疫苗的研发出现了一个突然而重大的发现——也就是突破。

sentences.en: So, could a vaccine for cancer soon become a reality?
sentences.zh: 那么，癌症疫苗很快会成为现实吗？

sentences.en: That’s what we’ll be finding out, as well as learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要去寻找的答案，同时我们还会学习一些有用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, if you like listening to 6 Minute English and want to read along at the same time, you can find a transcript for the programme on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，如果你喜欢听《6分钟英语》并想同时进行阅读，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到节目的文字稿。

sentences.en: Now I have a question for you, Beth. We’ve mentioned some of the most recent vaccines, but which disease did the first successful vaccine treat?
sentences.zh: 现在我有一个问题要问你，Beth。我们提到过一些最新的疫苗，但第一种成功治疗的疫苗是哪种疾病呢？

sentences.en: Was it: a) flu? b) polio? or c) smallpox?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 流感？b) 小儿麻痹症？还是 c) 天花？

sentences.en: I’m going to say polio. OK! Well, we’ll find out the correct answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 我要选小儿麻痹症。好的！嗯，我们会在节目结束时揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: You might wonder why the body’s immune system doesn’t fight cancer automatically.
sentences.zh: 你可能想知道为什么人体的免疫系统不会自动对抗癌症。

sentences.en: The reason is that cancer has clever ways of hiding from our natural defences, as Dr Meredith McKean, director of research at Tennessee Oncology, explained to BBC World Service programme, The Inquiry: There's been a number of studies that have demonstrated the different techniques that the cancer has developed to be able to put up signals or proteins, essentially, on the surface of the cancer cells, to tell the immune system, ‘Go away!
sentences.zh: 原因在于，癌症有巧妙的方法来隐藏以躲避我们的天然防御，正如田纳西肿瘤学研究主任Meredith McKean博士向BBC世界服务部节目《The Inquiry》所解释的那样：许多研究已经证明了癌症进化出的不同技术，基本上能够在癌细胞表面竖起信号或蛋白质，来告诉免疫系统：‘走开！’

sentences.en: There's nothing here to look at!’ And so it's actually been hijacking these receptors to essentially tell the immune system to kind of take the brakes off, and be more aggressive in fighting cancer.
sentences.zh: 这里没什么好看的！’因此，它实际上是在劫持这些受体，基本上是告诉免疫系统松开刹车，在抗癌时表现得更有攻击性。

sentences.en: That's really allowed a breakthrough with immune therapy over the past decade.
sentences.zh: 这确实让过去十年中的免疫疗法取得了突破。

sentences.en: Dr McKean says that a number of studies have demonstrated how cancer spreads.
sentences.zh: McKean博士表示，许多研究已经证明了癌症是如何扩散的。

sentences.en: She uses the phrase a number of to mean several, but it also makes her statement more convincing, because of course several studies are better than just one.
sentences.zh: 她用“a number of”这个短语来表示“几个”，但这也让她的陈述更具说服力，因为当然，几项研究总比仅仅一项要好。

sentences.en: Cancer cells switch off the immune system by pretending to be healthy cells.
sentences.zh: 癌细胞通过伪装成健康细胞来关闭免疫系统。

sentences.en: It’s like they’re saying Nothing to see here! – an informal phrase which can be used to encourage people to move or look away from something, either in a playful way, or to cover something up.
sentences.zh: 这就像它们在说“这里没什么好看的！”——这是一个非正式短语，可以用来鼓励人们离开或把视线从某事上移开，既可以是以开玩笑的方式，也可以是为了掩盖什么。

sentences.en: For example, a police officer at a crime scene might say, “Nothing to see here!” to move people on.
sentences.zh: 例如，犯罪现场的警察可能会说“这里没什么好看的！”来驱散人群。

sentences.en: So, in other words, cancer hijacks healthy cells – it takes control of something which doesn’t belong to it and uses it for its own advantage.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，癌症劫持了健康细胞——它控制了不属于自己的东西并为己所用。

sentences.en: So, how would a vaccine change things? Well, existing treatments, like chemotherapy, aggressively target the cancer, but also attack healthy tissue, creating unpleasant side effects.
sentences.zh: 那么，疫苗将如何改变现状呢？嗯，现有的治疗方法，如化疗，会强力攻击癌症，但也会攻击健康组织，从而产生令人不适的副作用。

sentences.en: New breakthrough vaccines, on the other hand, retrain the immune system to recognise cancer cells and eliminate those, and only those, naturally – even in patients with the disease already.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，新的突破性疫苗重新训练免疫系统去识别癌细胞并自然地消除它们——而且仅消除癌细胞，即使是对已经患病的患者也是如此。

sentences.en: Here’s, Professor Eduardo Sanchez, of the Anderson Cancer Center in Texas, explaining more to BBC World Service’s, The Inquiry: Basically the cancer cells are telling the immune system, ‘Don't attack me, don't eat me’, right?
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州安德森癌症中心的Eduardo Sanchez教授向BBC世界服务部的《The Inquiry》节目做了进一步解释：基本上癌细胞在告诉免疫系统，‘不要攻击我，不要吃我’，对吧？

sentences.en: The immune system has forgotten how to go about recognising those cancer cells, becoming blind to recognise those aberrations that cancer cells generate, and what we want to do with vaccines is to re-educate the immune system.
sentences.zh: 免疫系统已经忘记了如何去识别那些癌细胞，对癌细胞产生的那些畸变变得视而不见，而我们想通过疫苗做的事情就是重新教育免疫系统。

sentences.en: In cancer patients, the immune system is blind to cancerous growths – it completely fails to notice them or be aware of their danger, so the vaccine re-educates the immune system, or teaches it to behave, in a different way.
sentences.zh: 在癌症患者体内，免疫系统对肿瘤视而不见——它完全注意不到它们，也没有意识到它们的危险，因此疫苗重新教育了免疫系统，或者教导它以一种不同的方式行事。

sentences.en: To recap, some cancer treatments work by unblocking our blocked natural defences, whereas vaccines retrain the immune system to find and attack cancer cells naturally.
sentences.zh: 概括一下，一些癌症治疗的作用原理是解除我们受阻的天然防御，而疫苗则是重新训练免疫系统去自然地发现和攻击癌细胞。

sentences.en: Because these two approaches are quite different, they can be used together and individually.
sentences.zh: 由于这两种方法截然不同，它们既可以结合使用，也可以单独使用。

sentences.en: So, to answer my original question, Neil, a vaccine for cancer might not be too far away.
sentences.zh: 所以，回答我最初的问题，Neil，癌症疫苗或许已经并不遥远了。

sentences.en: But how about your question – isn’t it time you revealed the answer?
sentences.zh: 但你的问题呢——是不是该公布答案了？

sentences.en: I asked which disease was first successfully treated by a vaccine?
sentences.zh: 我问的是哪种疾病是被疫苗成功治疗的第一种疾病？

sentences.en: And I said polio. Was I right? You were wrong, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 我说的是小儿麻痹症。我猜对了吗？恐怕你猜错了。

sentences.en: The correct option was C, which is smallpox.
sentences.zh: 正确的选项是C，也就是天花。

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme, starting with breakthrough, a sudden, dramatic and important discovery.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们在本节目中学习的词汇，从breakthrough开始，意为突然的、戏剧性的重大发现。

sentences.en: A number of something means several, or many, and can add credibility to what you say.
sentences.zh: A number of某物意味着几个或许多，并且可以增加你所说话语的可信度。

sentences.en: The phrase, Nothing to see here! is used to discourage people from paying attention or looking too closely at something, or to move them away.
sentences.zh: 短语“这里没什么好看的！”用于劝阻人们不要关注或过分仔细地看某事，或者把他们支开。

sentences.en: If you hijack something, you use something that does not belong to you for your own benefit.
sentences.zh: 如果你劫持了某物，你就是在为自己的利益使用不属于你的东西。

sentences.en: Being blind to something means failing to notice it or recognise it as a threat.
sentences.zh: 对某事视而不见意味着未能注意到它或没有将它识别为威胁。

sentences.en: And finally, to re-educate means to teach somebody to think or behave in a new or different way.
sentences.zh: 最后，重新教育（re-educate）意味着教导某人以一种新的或不同的方式思考或行事。

sentences.en: Once again our six minutes are up, but if you’re hungry for more, head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, where you can find the worksheet for this programme, as well as a quiz.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，但如果你还想了解更多，请前往我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，在那里你可以找到本节目的练习册以及一个小测验。

sentences.en: Good luck and we’ll see you again soon. Bye for now!
sentences.zh: 祝你好运，我们很快再见。再见！

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
